external_claim.treatment: Read as a claim and checked against original contract/current code/existing original members; not authority to add acceptance gates.

method.coverage: Five existing 173 runtime raw streams/report/statistics plus all three backfill seeds' summary/held-before/quiet and held rows; 27 original member hashes; current C source bytes equal Git for 16 read paths.
method.excluded: No workload/native/statistics recomputation, no unchanged acceptance rerun, no source/status/CI modification. Current C has no raw yet. Existing ZIP whole verification was not repeated.

conclusion.requirement: The original section 9 mixed-load attribution requirement applies to P8-007/V20 now; it is not conditional on G8 or paid/live authorization.
conclusion.confirmed_gap: Mixed read/build C1/4/8/16 originals do not record actual operation-path database lock-acquisition waits. The separate backfill read-pool and BEGIN/ROLLBACK availability probe is real evidence but cannot be renamed as mixed-workload lock-wait attribution. Current C has the same missing observation seam.
conclusion.narrower_than_external_claim: The literal says queue+service+end-to-end, DB lock wait and worker contention. It does not specify a full per-request backend-span tree, a unique RPC-ID extension, timing every lock, or independent worker-capacity/admission/service distributions. Those are possible instrumentation designs, not additional mandatory gates. Existing client phases and held-worker evidence must be retained and credited at their actual scope.
conclusion.service_boundary: Existing dispatch/admission/call durations form an honest client-side decomposition. They do not separate backend queue from backend service. Requiring an additional backend-internal split is an interpretation of service, not an explicit extra word in the original clause. A completion claim must state the measured boundary and cannot relabel client call elapsed as pure backend service.
conclusion.task_010: No new four-concurrency one-hour matrix or mandatory repetition of every mixed-load attribution measure is imposed on P8-010. Its actual one-hour, cache/worker reuse, memory/queue and endpoint-parity observations remain valid for their original source. P8-007's real gap blocks downstream final completion through the original hard dependencies.
conclusion.status: No task closure; 163 done / 29 remaining. Original scoped helper successes remain successes of their recorded narrower scopes.

contract_anchors.clause: C15: index reports are user-triggered evidence, no continuously persisted product telemetry database; benchmark independently collects raw/resources.
C16: current target SHA evidence remains required with actual source applicability; no old record relabeling.

observed_fields.evidence: All five original statistics.json latency_scope explicitly says client observations include transport, admission and validation; no separated backend service or queue claim.
observed_fields.meaning: started-offered; call_started-started; finished-call_started; finished-offered; finished-scheduled. They retain all terminal denominators and are not backend-exclusive clocks.
Sampled executor occupancy/counts and bounded capacities; no accumulated wait or service duration. Not continuous peak and not per-operation attribution.
Actual build-stage timing/counters preserved. prepare/commit/postprocess elapsed includes work; it does not isolate mutex or SQLite lock wait.
128 quiet +128 held calls per seed across C1/4/8/16. Original rows explicitly deny separated backend queue/service timing. This is meaningful real CodeIndex/API progress evidence.

Actual four worker calls held at controlled fake provider, quiet/held request populations and terminal drain. This is actual contention/progress evidence; original requirement does not specifically demand worker-duration histograms.

One same-source probe per seed while provider is held, before all held query waves. Writer measurement includes BEGIN and ROLLBACK; it is not pure SQLite busy wait and not a timing distribution for actual mixed read/build operations.

production_seams.fact: run_cpu/run_async acquire admission and capacity, then execute work. Current ExecutionStats exposes counts/occupancy only.
capture_for_request uses the query pool before QueryHandle capture; capture obtains the CodeIndex read lock. Caller capture elapsed conflates these steps.
Actual CodeIndex read/write lock helpers have no timing.
Real index requests acquire a build gate before split build; no separate gate-wait record.
read_conn obtains pool read lock then pool.get(), with no acquisition-time record.
Actual write mutex and SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE are separate operations but their waits are not observed separately.

minimum_completion_path.immediate_no_source_work: Retain the original measured phases, error/timeout denominator, build stages, queue occupancy and held-worker controls. Append this gap disposition rather than changing their raw or passed statuses. Do not rename old fields.
minimum_completion_path.necessary_new_observation: Add bounded, explicitly scoped actual mixed-workload database acquisition observations. Use the real selected read-pool/write-mutex acquisition sites, preserve all failure/cancellation paths and record observed/not-observed separately. A run-level or per-operation bounded diagnostic is permissible; the original contract does not force an exhaustive span hierarchy.
minimum_completion_path.recommended_companion: If the claim will include separated backend service/queue, instrument the actual query executor's admission/capacity wait and executed closure duration rather than deriving them from client timestamps. This is the smallest unambiguous resolution of the service-boundary uncertainty, not a new latency threshold.
minimum_completion_path.sqlite_caveat: Time around BEGIN IMMEDIATE includes acquisition/SQL execution and must be named accordingly. Do not change SQLite busy_timeout/backoff/transaction semantics merely to count waits or report missing observations as zero. DB mutex/pool waits and SQLite engine busy wait are distinct.
minimum_completion_path.worker_caveat: Reuse existing real held-worker quiet/held controls for contention at that declared scope. Extra capacity/service timers are useful only if claimed; do not require an invented per-worker timing matrix.
minimum_completion_path.evidence: Bind diagnostics to the new exact build/observer, save raw snapshots/row linkage and original count/time/error denominators, preserve original C1/4/8/16 workload sizes, no best-of, original queue/deadline/raw budgets and cleanup. Add meaningful held-lock/queued-worker/cancel/error/no-observation controls before the actual source-bound mixed run. Existing uninstrumented raw cannot reconstruct absent waits.
minimum_completion_path.soak: Do not start another hour merely because section 9 has mixed-load timings. An eventual new-source soak decision depends on the patch's actual effect on the original memory/queue/cache/worker paths and the normal current-source workflow, not an invented extra attribution requirement.
minimum_completion_path.current_runs: Current C3ff original runs remain frozen and continue. No cancellation/restart/new workload performed or requested by this review.

scale_impact.actual_path: p8_scale.rs:640-645 calls CodeIndexBackend::build_index_report; runner.rs:131-132 sends the real index MCP tool over an in-process rmcp connection; handlers/core.rs executes the same gate/split build and underlying DB paths.
scale_impact.consequence: Instrumentation in shared cc-db or index handlers is inside the scale native executable and exercised build path, not an observer-only external edit. Even optional disabled diagnostics alter source/binary identity; an unchanged result cannot simply be rebranded as the new binary.
scale_impact.boundary: No patch exists yet, so no blanket claim that all scale evidence must rerun and no blanket source-equivalence claim is justified. Preserve ongoing C scale and all its samples at C. A future diff-specific closure review must identify whether/how measured path and enabled diagnostic behavior change; no mixing new/old shard populations, counts or timings.
scale_impact.no_new_gates: This review adds no G8, live provider, paid call, 4x-hour soak, exhaustive lock tracing, new performance margin, or requirement to reach configured C as observed peak.

peer_contract_review.scope: Independent original contract interpretation only, not this fresh raw readback or product acceptance.

limitations: The external record's claim of absent fully separated backend data is factually consistent; its assertion that every listed internal timing is mandatory needs the narrower literal/measurement distinction above.
No current C raw exists at last official poll09:44:59; conclusions about its missing fields derive from exact current code, not fabricated execution.
A bounded observation success is not stable-tail certification or causal speedup.
Formal task completion remains false; original definitions, dependencies and historical evidence are unchanged.
